briefing.text: The hypothesis is about miRNA expression levels (miR-452, miR-766, miR-1180). Before analysing, list every provided file and check whether any of them holds miRNA or mRNA expression values (e.g. a data_mirna*, data_expression* or data_mrna* table, or MIR* rows in any data matrix). The listed files (clinical sample, discrete CNA, hg19 seg, mutations, gene panel matrix) look like DNA-level targeted-panel data; confirm this yourself rather than assuming it.
briefing.reason: Whether the measured variable exists at all determines which label is even possible, so this check has to come first.

briefing.text: The hypothesis compares HCA and HCC with normal liver. Tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS and ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt and check whether any normal-liver samples with profiled values exist. Matched-normal barcodes (e.g. _N) in the mutation file are used only for somatic calling and are not a normal-tissue comparison group.
briefing.reason: Without a normal-liver group, the 'vs normal liver' contrast cannot be computed, and a team could mistake matched-normal IDs for a comparison group.

briefing.text: Do not use copy-number gain or amplification (data_cna.txt, seg.mean) or mutations in a miRNA host gene as a stand-in for miRNA upregulation. Copy number does not reliably track expression, and CNA calls are made relative to the tumour's matched normal, so they are not an expression comparison against normal liver.
briefing.reason: CNA and seg files are the tempting proxy here. Using them would give an invalid True or False.

briefing.text: Apply the task's label definitions strictly. 'False' requires that the three miRNAs were actually measured in HCA, HCC and normal liver and showed no difference or an opposite one. Lacking the relevant variables is not evidence against the claim. Base the label only on variables present in the provided files, not on published findings.
briefing.reason: This stops a team from confusing 'cannot test' with 'contradicted', or from filling the gap with outside knowledge.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed the only possible evidence would be a miRNA/expression table, and that copy-number at miRNA loci cannot count as evidence of upregulation; neither tested whether the segment file reaches those loci at all.

Both assumed the matched normal barcodes (_N) in the mutation file are not a usable normal-liver comparison group; this is sound (they are germline references for variant calling, with no expression values), but neither team reported checking whether any normal sample appears as its own sample in any file.
unused_evidence: data_cna_hg19.seg (genome segment log-ratios) was only described, not examined for coverage at the three miRNA loci; it is panel-derived, so it is unlikely to cover them, and copy number is not expression in any case. Ignoring it cannot plausibly move the label from Not verifiable to True or False.
TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS, SAMPLE_ORIGIN and SAMPLE_COLLECTION_METHOD are irrelevant to miRNA expression.
unresolved_weak_points: Team B named CNA gain at miRNA loci as a loose proxy and rejected it on principle without checking whether the seg/CNA data even cover those loci. Team A said it had no weak point. Neither left a substantive gap.
second_readings: 'Significantly upregulated versus normal liver' could be read as HCA vs HCC tumour vs tumour, but the hypothesis explicitly names normal liver as the reference, and that group and any expression outcome are absent under every reading. No second reading makes the claim testable here.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed Not verifiable label highly. The data hold only 19 tumour samples (10 HCC, 9 LIAD), with panel mutations and copy number. There is no miRNA or other expression variable and no normal-liver group, and I can find no reading or unused file that would supply either. So I have no question worth asking.
